subject: How can one action trigger two UI changes, one instant, and one waiting for computation to finish?

messages.author: 3b718630a63ab359
messages.subject: How can one action trigger two UI changes, one instant, and one waiting for computation to finish?
parts:
I want to add a spinning wheel while model is running, and then display model plots when it's done. But I realize that, if the modeling (and of course the spinning wheel as well) is triggered by a button click, although I have two separate observe functions for the modeling and spinning wheel, the UI will not refresh until both of them finish. Is there anyway to have a walk around?

Thanks!!!

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: How can one action trigger two UI changes, one instant, and one waiting for computation to finish?
parts:
It's true that outputs hold themselves until all of them are ready. But the same does not apply to session$sendCustomMessage. You can set up an observer that sets the spinning wheel via sendCustomMessage, and give it a higher priority, like so:

progressObserver <- observe({
  input$button
  isolate({
    session$sendCustomMessage("progress", ...)
  })
})
progressObserver$setPriority(10)

This will ensure that the custom message will be sent before executing any other observers that are scheduled at the same time.

The actual implementation of the spinning wheel has to be done in JavaScript, we don't have that as a component yet.

messages.subject: Re: How can one action trigger two UI changes, one instant, and one waiting for computation to finish?
parts:
I believe the title of this thread relates to what I am trying to do.  To explain my situation, I have two observe functions for which I would like to get the first one to execute fully before having the second one execute. Both have a common input dependency, but the second also relies on an input value that gets modified based on an updateSelectInput statement in the first observe statement.  To show this in code:

First
    datasetInputPre <- observe({
       input$myDataset
      (Statements to create varChoices)
      updateSelectInput(session, "myChoices", "My Label", c("", myChoices), selected="") 
       (Additional statements)
    }, priority=10)

Second
    datasetInputSecond <- observe({
       input$myDataset

      STATEMENTS TO HANDLE NULL AND "" CASES FOR input$myvar 
      chosen<-input$myChoices
    })

When I load myDataset for the first time, it works, but when I change the value of myDataset, the second observe statement uses the selected non-missing variable from the first time, so I get an error even though I intend to reset variable chosen to "".  How do I tell R to finish all processing with the first observe before jumping to the second?  I tried using session$sendCustomMessage as shown in the reply but couldn't get it to work.

I realize that technically this can be avoided by combining the two observe statements into one.  Eventually, I want to replace the first observe statement with a RenderUI call and give that priority over the second observe statement.  This is because depending on the value of input$myDataset, I wish to have a second selectInput for another subset of choices.
